The paper presents the Integrated Interval Mahalanobis Classification System (IIMCS) for classifying the vibrational quality of metallic turbine blades under measurement uncertainty.
IIMCS employs a Monte Carlo method framework to propagate the measurement uncertainty into the Mahalanobis distance space, resulting in the Interval Mahalanobis Distance (IMD).

IIMCS provides a reliability indicator 'r' that ranges from -1 to 1, with the sign indicating whether the sample is classified as 'Bad' or 'Good', and the absolute value representing the confidence level of the classification.
The case study on equiaxed nickel alloy first-stage turbine blades had a dataset of 232 blades, with 193 healthy and 39 defective blades.
Vibration testing was conducted in the frequency range of [3, 38] kHz, and 15 resonance frequencies (f1 to f15) were identified for further analysis.
The use of the optimal feature subset (f2, f4, f14, f15) resulted in a significantly narrower range of IMD values compared to using the full set of 15 features.
The classification accuracy on the testing dataset was 97.85%, with only 2 misclassifications observed.
The reliability indicator 'r' was able to identify one of the misclassified blades (blade 87) as having a low reliability value of -0.78, indicating a low confidence in classifying it as 'Good'.

The main novelties of IIMCS are the implementation of a Monte Carlo method to propagate measurement uncertainty and the introduction of a reliability indicator to assess the confidence in the classification results.

IIMCS addresses the challenges of the original Mahalanobis-Taguchi System (MTS) by employing BPSO for feature selection, integrating the threshold determination as part of the feature selection process, and accounting for measurement uncertainty.
The IIMCS methodology can be potentially applied to other complex-shaped metal parts or components that require non-destructive testing and quality classification under measurement uncertainty.
The ICON project DETECT-ION (HBC.2017.0603) and the SIM research program MacroModelMat (M3) funded by the Flemish government agency VLAIO supported this research.
Vibrant Corporation provided the anonymous datasets of the turbine blades used in the case study.
The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the IIMCS approach in classifying the vibrational quality of metallic turbine blades with high accuracy and reliability.

The integration of Interval Mahalanobis Distance and the reliability indicator in IIMCS represents a significant advancement in addressing measurement uncertainty in non-destructive testing and quality classification.
